slides.headline: Meshy plugged its AI into a chat assistant
body: Meshy is one of the biggest AI 3D-modeling tools: you type a description or upload a picture, and it builds a 3D model.
This week it released a plugin for Hermes Agent, so you can now make 3D models just by chatting.

slides.headline: Wait, what’s Hermes Agent?
body: It’s a free, open-source AI assistant made by Nous Research. Think ChatGPT, but you can plug extra tools into it.
Meshy’s plugin is one of those tools. Once it’s installed, Hermes can make and fix 3D models for you, right in the chat.

slides.headline: Chat in, 3MF out
hits: You describe the part or figure in plain English
It checks for print problems and repairs them
Scales it to real size, exports a 3MF for your slicer

slides.headline: AI models usually fail as prints
body: Holes in the mesh, paper-thin walls and random scale make most AI models a pain to print.
This plugin checks and repairs those problems before you ever open your slicer.

slides.headline: What does it cost?
body: The plugin is free to install. Making models uses Meshy credits, so you need a paid Meshy plan.
Hermes shows you the credit cost and waits for your OK before every job. Files save as STL, OBJ, 3MF and more.

slides.headline: How we’d use it
body: We already make models with hi3D and Claude, then slice in OrcaSlicer for our Bambu and Snapmaker printers.
slides.take: Auto-repair is the step everyone skips. If Meshy’s fix holds up on real prints, it saves hours of cleanup.
